title: Constructibility descends through surjective pullback
statement: Let $u:V\to U$ be a surjective morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism] of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then $F$ is constructible if and only if $u^{-1}F$ is constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, assertion (3), specialized to finite commutative rings

proof.text: Assume $F$ constructible in the precise sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Choose its finite stratification $(i_k:Z_k\to U)_{k<n}$ with constructible images $T_k$ and finite locally constant module restrictions. By [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification], the base changes $i'_k:Z_k\times_U V\to V$ form a stratification with images $u^{-1}(T_k)$. Each image is constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage], applied to $u$ and $T_k$. Put $v_k:Z_k\times_U V\to Z_k$. Clauses (1)--(2) of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identify constant-coefficient module inverse image with sheaf pullback. Since $u i'_k=i_k v_k$, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] gives $(i'_k)^{-1}u^{-1}F\cong v_k^{-1}i_k^{-1}F$ as module sheaves. By (1) iff (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], $i_k^{-1}F$ is locally constant with finite stalks in the coefficient category $\mathrm{Mod}_\Lambda$. Applying [lemma-constructible-pullback-locally-constant] and [lemma-constructible-pullback-finite] to $v_k$ preserves these two properties. By [lemma-constructible-iso-invariance] and the reverse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values], $(i'_k)^{-1}u^{-1}F$ has finite constant module values on an etale covering. This verifies both conditions of [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] on the pulled-back strata. Thus $u^{-1}F$ is constructible. This argument works for any scheme morphism, without surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 095G, label lemma-pullback-constructible; Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, first sentence

proof.text: Assume $u^{-1}F$ constructible. The finite ring $\Lambda$ is Noetherian, since an ascending chain of ideals is a chain of subsets of a finite set and therefore stabilizes. Fix the coefficient universe $u+1$ for $U,V:\mathrm{Scheme}_u$ and all module values and small diagrams below. More generally let $H$ be any module sheaf on $U$ with $u^{-1}H$ constructible. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible] write $H$ as the colimit of a diagram $(H_a)$ of constructible module sheaves indexed by a small filtered category $A$, with legs $a_a:H_a\to H$. Clause (3) of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes module inverse image a left adjoint. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $(u^{-1}H,(u^{-1}a_a))$ is a colimit of the pulled-back diagram. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-large-colimit-factorization] on the qcqs scheme $V$ to the identity of the constructible sheaf $u^{-1}H$. It factors as $u^{-1}H\xrightarrow{s}u^{-1}H_a\xrightarrow{u^{-1}a_a}u^{-1}H$ for some $a$, with composite identity. Thus $u^{-1}a_a$ is a split epimorphism.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, filtered-colimit paragraph; Tag 03SA, label lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible (3); Tag 09Z4, label lemma-constructible-is-compact; Categories Tag 0038

proof.text: For the map $a_a:H_a\to H$ selected in step 2, set $Q=\operatorname{Coker}(a_a)$ in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Exactness of module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives $u^{-1}Q=\operatorname{Coker}(u^{-1}a_a)=0$. For each point $y$ of $U$, surjectivity [def-weil-surjective-morphism] supplies $x$ of $V$ over $y$; choose an algebraic closure $\Omega_x$ of $\kappa(x)$ and the resulting geometric point $\bar x$ of $V$. The composite $\bar y=u\bar x$ is a geometric point above $y$. Module inverse image is compatible with abelian inverse image, so [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $Q$ identifies $Q_{\bar y}$ with $(u^{-1}Q)_{\bar x}=0$. The family of these $\bar y$ covers $U$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] to the underlying map $Q\to0$: all its stalk maps are bijections of singleton sets, hence it is an isomorphism. For every etale object $W$, the bijection $Q(W)\to0(W)$ says that $Q(W)$ has only its zero section. Its inverse sends zero to zero and therefore preserves addition and every $\Lambda$-scalar action, compatibly with restrictions. Thus $Q\cong0$ as a module sheaf. Consequently $a_a$ is an epimorphism. Steps 2--3 therefore give, for every such $H$, a constructible sheaf mapping epimorphically to $H$.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, stalk argument; Tags 03Q1, label lemma-stalk-pullback (3), and 03PU, label theorem-exactness-stalks

proof.text: Apply steps 2--3 first to $H=F$, obtaining an epimorphism $p:G\to F$ with $G$ constructible. Put $K=\operatorname{Ker}(p)$. Exactness [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $u^{-1}K$ with $\operatorname{Ker}(u^{-1}p)$. The source $u^{-1}G$ is constructible by the arbitrary-morphism argument of step 1, and the target $u^{-1}F$ is constructible by hypothesis. The kernel clause of [thm-constructible-serre], on $V$ with the same finite commutative coefficient ring, makes $u^{-1}K$ constructible. Apply the already proved general conclusion of steps 2--3 to $H=K$; this gives an epimorphism $r:C\to K$ with $C$ constructible. This second application is not an invocation of the theorem being proved: steps 2--3 only establish a constructible quotient presentation, not constructibility of $H$.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, final paragraph (kernel case); Tag 03RZ, label lemma-constructible-abelian (3)

proof.text: Let $i:K\to G$ be the kernel inclusion. Since $r$ is an epimorphism, the image of $ir:C\to G$ is exactly $K=\operatorname{Ker}(p)$. Since $p$ is an epimorphism, it follows in the abelian category [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] that $F\cong\operatorname{Coker}(ir)$. Explicitly, a map out of $G$ annihilates $ir$ exactly when it annihilates $i$, because $r$ is epi; the cokernel of the kernel inclusion of the epimorphism $p$ is $p$. Both $C$ and $G$ are constructible, so the cokernel clause of [thm-constructible-serre] makes $F$ constructible. Together with step 1 this proves the equivalence.

source.place: Tag 095Q, label lemma-check-constructible, last sentence; Tag 03RZ, label lemma-constructible-abelian (3)
